topic: K1 prove root-n W1 estimation of the quotient latent-effect law in the fixed-k Virk-Mazaheri-Wu proxy model through eigenvalue collisions. K2 construct honest cluster-adaptive W1 confidence sets. K3 prove labeled-weight error min{1,(sqrt(n)delta)^-1}. K4 match both regimes by local lower bounds. Include the explicit full-rank k=2 collision witness and PROTECT stage-III NSCLC consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: In the witness, proxy matrices remain nonsingular while effects .25-epsilon and .25+epsilon merge. Observable operators and auxiliary moments fluctuate at root-n scale. For a delta-wide cluster, projector-mass error of order 1/(sqrt(n)delta) is transported only across distance delta, suggesting root-n W1 cancellation even though labels fail. Bauer-Fike localization and aggregate cluster projectors provide a plausible proof spine. Exact collision, unequal weights, and delta near n^-1/2 showed no immediate contradiction; complex empirical eigenvalues remain unresolved. Separated submodels also provide a standard Gaussian local lower bound. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a uniform operator-to-positive-measure perturbation lemma through simultaneous cluster merges and splits, including nonreal empirical spectra, then calibrate honest clustering and a matching local experiment. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaust the two-by-two witness under all root-n moment perturbations. Stop if quotient W1 error contains any inverse-epsilon factor or construct two statistically root-n-close admissible operators whose quotient laws are separated by more than root-n.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the fixed-k Virk–Mazaheri–Wu proxy moments be mapped to the quotient latent-effect law at a uniform root-n W1 rate through arbitrary effect collisions, including nonreal empirical spectra, by replacing labeled eigenvectors with aggregate spectral projectors and a total positivity-preserving repair?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Virk–Mazaheri–Wu localizes eigenvalues at root-n scale, yet its feature-row and mixture-weight theorem requires simple separated effects and inherits a 1/δ eigenvector factor. At a merge, individual projectors and labels are discontinuous although their cluster sum is stable; with a real nonsymmetric empirical operator, a root-n perturbation can also split a repeated real eigenvalue into a complex pair. The prior-proposal record independently flags latent effect groups as outside an accepted estimator's scope, treats repeated-eigenspace invariance as necessary for a total spectral map, and records that an algebraic population inverse without a positivity event or regularization is not a computable estimator. New work must therefore control simultaneous cluster merges and splits, transport unstable mass only over the within-cluster diameter, and return a positive real probability measure on every sample without hiding an eigengap assumption.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A deterministic operator-to-positive-measure perturbation lemma and a total estimator ν_hat such that, over a fixed-k VMW class with bounded observations, latent-arm positivity, a proxy singular-value margin, and bounded similarity condition number, P{W1(ν_hat,ν)>C√(log(1/η)/n)}≤η uniformly without an effect eigengap, including conjugate empirical eigenpairs, while reducing to componentwise root-n recovery in separated clusters.

writing_exemplar.why: It defines the observable quotient operator, conditioning constants, separated perturbation theorem, and complex-bifurcation boundary that the new result must extend.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: spectral identification of latent effects -> separated first-order recovery fails at collisions -> estimate the quotient law through stable cluster geometry

method_exemplars.technique: Replace individual eigenvectors by contour-defined Riesz projectors and cluster traces or bilinear projector functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Aggregate projectors remain meaningful through internal multiplicity, exactly matching the quotient law's merger of equal-effect labels.

method_exemplars.technique: Use condition-number-sensitive localization to assign every empirical root to a root-n neighborhood of the real population support before cluster collapse.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies gap-free support localization even though it does not itself recover positive masses or stable labels.

method_exemplars.technique: Project noisy algebraic summaries onto a positive truncated-moment cone before extracting a finite atomic measure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired estimator likewise must turn noisy roots and residues that may be complex or signed into a valid probability law without losing its Wasserstein rate.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the matching local minimax risks for the VMW quotient law and for effect-ordered component weights near a two-effect collision, and in particular is the labeled-weight frontier min{1,(√nδ)⁻¹} while quotient-law W1 risk remains root-n?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary finite-mixture collision rates do not automatically transfer because VMW observes a root-n estimable operator that encodes effect support directly; this may make its quotient law much easier than deconvolution. Conversely, a labeled-weight lower bound must neutralize the direct root-n information about p in E[X]=Bp by jointly perturbing B, p, the arm-specific proxy factors, and latent arm probabilities along a factorization-preserving direction whose observed score is attenuated by δ. Prior reviewers independently require a positive small-dimensional witness with a nonzero rank minor and a same-class contiguity converse, and warn that a generic hypothesis-independent scaling channel can deliver the wrong product-type separation. The presolved 2-by-2 witness has therefore not discharged the bottleneck until every probability, conditional independence, full-rank margin, KL expansion, and quotient separation is checked under the least-favorable tangent.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A pair of matched local minimax theorems proving inf_νhat sup_P E[W1(ν_hat,ν_P)]≥c/√n and, at nearest-neighbor gap δ, inf_phat sup_P E[||p_hat−p||]≥c min{1,(√nδ)⁻¹}, together with attaining cluster-projector upper bounds and a verified unequal-weight k=2 interior witness having p=(0.4,0.6), P(T=1|U)=(0.4,0.6), B=[[1,1],[0.2,0.8]], arm-specific second rows (0.3,0.7) and (0.35,0.75), and effects 0.25−ε and 0.25+ε while all proxy determinants and arm probabilities remain uniformly nonzero.

writing_exemplar.why: It organizes a collision question around pointwise versus local-uniform behavior and pairs rate claims with explicit minimax converses.

method_exemplars.technique: Build a two-point functional modulus with explicit KL or Hellinger control along a least-favorable factorization-preserving VMW path.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly converts one admissible local path into separate lower bounds for quotient W1 and labeled weights.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand the observed model along collision tangents and determine which score derivatives vanish before choosing the local scale.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired labeled-weight frontier depends on a first-order loss of information proportional to δ rather than on a generic mixture singularity.

method_exemplars.technique: Use proxy conditional-independence factorizations and explicit rank minors to keep the local alternatives inside a causally admissible full-rank model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The converse is relevant only if its statistically close alternatives remain genuine proxy causal laws rather than arbitrary nearby matrices.

Define a norm, a simultaneous-region radius r_alpha, and the set diameter/Hausdorff metric

open_problems.why_unsolved: A delta-method ellipsoid for labeled eigenpairs divides by the smallest effect gap and undercovers at a merge, whereas a constant full-alphabet fallback is formally honest but scientifically empty. Coverage is additionally nonregular when the empirical cluster partition changes, eigenvalues form conjugate pairs, or the optimal transport plan is nonunique. Existing Wasserstein confidence-set results concern density models or inference for a distance between topic-model mixtures, not inversion of a nonnormal causal quotient operator. The prior-proposal record reinforces the missing ingredients: define a simultaneous input-region radius and output metric, calibrate uniformly over collision regimes, and avoid treating a constant set as adaptation. Data-driven clustering may describe which coordinates are reported, but it cannot be an unaccounted preliminary event on which coverage is conditioned.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence set C_n⊂P_k(R) satisfying inf_P P_P{ν(P)∈C_n}≥1−α and diam_W1(C_n)=O_P(n⁻¹ᐟ²) uniformly over the conditioned fixed-k VMW class, with simultaneous root-n support intervals and O(min{1,(√nδ)⁻¹}) weight intervals for separated atoms, root-n aggregate-mass intervals for unresolved clusters, and valid coverage across merge/split boundaries without a preliminary separation event.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly separates honesty, adaptive diameter, constructive upper bounds, and testing-based impossibility under Wasserstein loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Center an honest set at an adaptive estimator and control its diameter by tests over the union of spectral strata.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the honesty-versus-adaptation architecture needed when the unknown effect partition changes at collisions.

method_exemplars.technique: Use directional limits and data-driven critical values for discrete Wasserstein functionals with nonunique optimal-transport geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest inferential treatment of nonsmooth discrete Wasserstein geometry, although the VMW input is an estimated operator rather than a topic simplex.

method_exemplars.technique: Define reported cluster masses through aggregate spectral projectors that stay stable under internal multiplicity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies the cluster-level coordinates that can remain inferentially meaningful when component labels cannot.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what explicit estimand and assumption correspondence can collision-robust VMW quotient-law inference be used for the stage-III NSCLC PROTECT setting with censored survival and mixed clinical proxies, and when is such a correspondence impossible?

source_refs.claim: PROTECT uses a parametric structural model and proxy measurements of latent patient fitness in 504 stage-III NSCLC patients to estimate hazard-based average and individual treatment effects under unobserved confounding.
source_refs.author: Wouter A. C. van Amsterdam et al.

source_refs.claim: VMW assumes a fixed finite latent class, proxy conditional independences, full-rank feature matrices, latent-arm positivity, and bounded moment contributions; it does not treat survival censoring or NSCLC data.
source_refs.author: Hamza Virk, Bijan Mazaheri, Yihren Wu

source_refs.claim: The SPO causal-mixture target is defined through a discrete latent class and observable multilinear moments, which is not automatically the continuous latent-fitness target used by PROTECT.
source_refs.author: Bijan Mazaheri, Chandler Squires, Caroline Uhler

source_refs.claim: Proxy identification requires stated conditional-independence and rank assumptions, so clinical proxy semantics alone do not establish that a spectral proxy model applies.
source_refs.author: Wang Miao, Zhi Geng, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: PROTECT estimates hazard-based individual effects using a parametric continuous-latent DAG, MCMC, and censored clinical outcomes, whereas VMW targets a finite atomic law of differences in conditional potential-outcome means from bounded cross-moments. The clinical and spectral estimands, the meanings of the two proxy sets, censoring assumptions, and positivity/rank conditions therefore do not coincide automatically. Neither paper proves the required bridge: VMW has no survival or NSCLC analysis, while PROTECT has no spectral-collision theory. Without a correspondence theorem or counterexample, calling PROTECT a validation of the spectral estimator would overstate the evidence and could turn a safe law-level result into unsupported patient-level recommendations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A correspondence theorem mapping a prespecified finite fitness stratification and an inverse-censoring-weighted bounded survival functional into the VMW observable moments while verifying conditional independence, full rank, positivity, and censoring conditions, or a counterexample proving that no such mapping follows from the PROTECT DAG and stated model assumptions; either outcome must delimit which aggregate law-level clinical claims remain valid.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the actual clinical estimand, DAG, proxy interpretation, cohort size, censoring context, uncertainty, and limitations that a consumer bridge must preserve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: unobserved fitness confounds treatment choice -> clinical proxies support a structured latent model -> a theorem must delimit when finite spectral effect-law inference is an admissible extension

method_exemplars.technique: Translate domain proxy statements into testable matrix-rank and conditional-independence conditions for a latent causal law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the identification discipline needed to distinguish clinical proxy plausibility from a valid two-proxy causal factorization.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct the compressed quotient operator from bounded observable cross-moments after any justified censoring transformation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the destination estimator whose finite-latent, bounded-moment, and rank requirements must be reconciled with the PROTECT observation model.

literature_map:
Virk–Mazaheri–Wu 2026 is the exact anchor: a compressed observable proxy operator has the latent-effect support as its spectrum.
Mazaheri–Squires–Uhler 2025 is the scalar-moment/Hankel predecessor and identifies causal mixtures, but does not give collision-uniform inference.
Miao–Geng–Tchetgen Tchetgen 2018 anchors two-proxy rank identification and the need to keep lower-bound paths inside an admissible causal model.
Bauer–Fike 1960 gives gap-free eigenvalue localization for diagonalizable population operators but not stable labels, masses, or positivity.
Kato 1995 supplies the key collision object: aggregate Riesz projectors for externally isolated clusters.
Anandkumar et al. 2014 represents robust componentwise spectral latent-variable recovery whose separation logic does not handle merges.
Wu–Yang 2020 shows how projection of noisy algebraic summaries onto a feasible moment cone can repair invalid empirical roots.
Heinrich–Kahn 2018 separates pointwise root-n from slower local-uniform finite-mixture rates and is the closest lower-bound narrative.
Ho–Nguyen 2016 and Ho et al. 2022 show how weak component separation creates derivative singularities, slow labeled rates, and pile-up.
Those ordinary-mixture rates need not transfer to VMW because the VMW operator itself is estimable at root-n and encodes effect support directly.
Deo–Randrianarisoa 2023 and Robins–van der Vaart 2006 supply honesty/adaptation frameworks, but neither treats changing nonnormal spectral strata.
Bing–Bunea–Niles-Weed 2025 gives inference for discrete Wasserstein functionals with nonsmooth transport geometry, adjacent to but distinct from operator collision.
Van Amsterdam et al. 2022 is the protected stage-III NSCLC consumer: its hazard estimand, continuous latent fitness model, censoring, and n=504 require an explicit bridge before application.
